why: A crystal chain proves a theorem about the trust-ir trustc emits for a shipped body.
Where that body is a match over a kernel enum, the emitted IR names no variants -- it
switches on the NUMERIC DISCRIMINANT, and Clean's side of the proof encodes the same
numbers (clean_mode_tag, level_kind_tag). Before this pin that mapping appeared in the
Rust source nowhere at all. The language guarantees the VALUES given a declaration order
(Reference: unspecified first discriminant is 0, each later one is previous + 1); nothing
guaranteed the ORDER. Reordering two variants -- a refactor that changes no behaviour of
the Rust program -- moves Cubical off 2 while the registered module, the recorded fixture
and every gate over them stay byte-identical, and the chain goes on reporting green while
proving something false about the shipped body.
enforced_by: scripts/check_enum_tag_pin.py -- this manifest vs the enum sources, the spec tag defs and the recorded artifacts; wired into scripts/local_gate.sh --fast

discriminant == declaration index, so the ABI tag and serde's variant index cannot diverge

every aggregate-constant tag `const <ir_type> { k }` is a pinned discriminant

ir_type_note: ir_type is the type token in the emitted text (`load enum.13, ptr %0`).
CORRECTED 2026-08-19: this note read "crystal_a1_lineage's CFG parser does NOT read it
-- emitted_cfg_parse.rs takes t.last() for `load` (the POINTER register) and
t.get(2)/t.get(3) for `extractfield`, dropping the type at t.get(1). Pinning it here is
the only place the token is read at all." That was true when written and the
operand-completeness audit closed it the same day: `load_tys` and `extract_tys` are now
lanes of the CFG gate, so the token is compared spec-against-artifact on every run. The
audit's first act was to turn the flagship RED -- ir_h2_b0 loaded `ir_tLevel`
(IRTy.enum_ 0) where this manifest says enum.13 -- and the registered module was
corrected to `ir_h2_tmode : IRTy := IRTy.enum_ ir_d13`, which is what this pin asserts.
This pin is therefore no longer the ONLY reader, and it is not redundant either: it
reads the token against the ENUM DECLARATION, where the lane reads it against the
registered spec. It is still a RECORDED artifact value: a legitimate re-dump can
renumber it, and when it does this gate fires so a human looks, which is the intended
behaviour and not a false alarm.

repr_exception: PAYLOAD-BEARING, so `as u8` does not apply and #[repr(u8)] would be a LAYOUT change to
the kernel's hottest type. It is pinned by declaration order here instead. Taking the
repr would move the emitted bytes on the DESIGNATED crystal target and stale every
fixtures/level_is_zero.a0.json, which pins 4 PASS / 2 FAIL). That flip needs its own
differential measurement and a re-dump; this gate closes the reorder hole without it.
Residual, stated rather than smoothed: Level's tag ENCODING (u8 at aggregate field 0)
is still rustc's choice, not a source-level guarantee.

what_changes: Adding #[repr(u8)] makes trustc's THIR lowering carry a repr HINT it did not carry before:
trust-thir-lower/src/lib.rs enum_repr_hint(adt) -> EnumDef::with_repr, so EnumDef.repr goes
None -> Some(U8) for CleanMode, SourceSystem and ExprPathStep in the emitted module.
why_it_is_a_strengthening: Without a hint, trust's interpreter derives the tag width from the DISCRIMINANT RANGE:
EnumDef::canonical_tag_repr() falls through to EnumTagRepr::smallest_for(min, max)
(trust-ir/src/ty.rs:1001-1011). So the model's `u8` agreed with the emitted
`extractfield u8` only because the values happened to fit in a byte; a single wide
discriminant would have silently widened the MODEL while the emitted body kept reading one
byte. With the hint present the interpreter instead enforces `hint.fits(d)` for every
discriminant and returns None -- a hard interpreter error, and a lowering DECLINE at
registration -- rather than widening. That is a real gap closed, not an annotation.
what_must_be_re_measured: Body TEXT is unaffected: the recorded .trust-ir.txt fixtures are function bodies and carry
no enum def, so every link-2a CFG gate compares the same bytes it compared before.
Per-body LINEAGE is affected: body_lineage_digest frames mini_module.stable_digest()
(trust-thir-lower/src/lineage.rs:171-192) and the mini-module carries the type table, so the
three fieldless-enum chains -- has_cubical_layer, from_source_system, expr_path_step_clone --
will mint NEW lineage digests on the next dump. Re-dump and re-run
scripts/crystal_fixture_freshness.py, then supersede those three .lineage.json records the

niche_descriptor_finding.context: data/crystal_layout_divergence_2026-08-18.json: 115 of 208 enum defs in this crate carry a Niche descriptor, so `tag at field 0` is not a safe default.
niche_descriptor_finding.do_the_chained_bodies_assume_it: YES, all six recorded artifacts do: every one reads the discriminant as `extractfield u8 %v, 0` on the enum aggregate. A niche-encoded enum has no separate tag field -- the discriminant is recovered from a payload value -- so that instruction would be reading a payload byte.
niche_descriptor_finding.after_this_change: For the three FIELDLESS enums the assumption is now guaranteed by the source rather than inferred: a #[repr(u8)] fieldless enum IS a u8, there is no payload for a niche to live in, and crystal_tag_pin.rs asserts size_of == 1 at compile time.
niche_descriptor_finding.residual: level::Level is payload-bearing and takes no repr here, so its tag encoding (Direct, u8, aggregate field 0) remains rustc's choice, evidenced only by the recorded artifact. It is exactly the class the 115 Niche descriptors warn about. Closing it means flipping Level to #[repr(u8)] behind a differential measurement -- a separate change, named in the level/mod.rs CRYSTAL TAG PIN comment.
niche_descriptor_finding.what_the_text_form_cannot_show: The trust-ir TEXT printer emits no enum layout descriptor at all (docs/CRYSTAL_STATUS.md 4h.5), so no committed .trust-ir.txt fixture can answer Direct-vs-Niche for any of these four enums. Deciding it requires the BINARY dump.

that is no longer shipped -- is closed by PINNING DECLARATION ORDER, and that costs zero
bytes of clean-kernel source. It is here, enforced, today.

and goes RED: the body the spec module transcribes may no longer be the body the producer
emits, and no fixture in the tree can say. Clearing it needs a live trustc dump and a new
